name: better-accessibility
description: Reviews and fixes keyboard and focus behavior, ARIA, accessible names, forms, screen-reader announcements, motion and zoom in your project against WCAG 2.2.

interface.shortDescription: Focus, keyboard, ARIA, forms and screen readers

name: better-colors
description: Helps you build and check a color system for your project. It generates palettes, names semantic tokens, converts between formats and measures contrast.

interface.shortDescription: Building, naming and applying color systems

name: better-interface
description: Reviews screens and flows across accessibility, layout, writing, typography, color and UI polish. Routes change-review requests to an explicit interface-review invocation; consolidates its authorized handoff.

name: better-layout
description: Helps with grouping, alignment, reading order, responsive structure and room for translated text, so a layout holds up when it is resized, translated or mirrored.

interface.shortDescription: Structure, grouping, alignment and adaptive layout

name: better-typography
description: Sets and reviews how text renders in your product, from the type scale and spacing to font features, wrapping, truncation and punctuation.

interface.shortDescription: Fonts, type scales, spacing and wrapping

name: better-ui
description: Polishes the surfaces, icons and motion in your project with exact values for border radius, optical alignment, shadows, icon states and animation.

interface.shortDescription: Design engineering details for polished interfaces

name: better-writing
description: Writes and reviews your interface copy, from labels and errors to empty states and confirmations, so it matches your product's voice and tells people what to do next.

interface.shortDescription: UX writing, interface copy and microcopy

name: break
description: Renders a component you choose under every scenario that can reach it on a temporary page and stress tests it.

interface.shortDescription: Render one component under hostile inputs and report what breaks

name: build-design
description: Builds an approved browser prototype, Markdown screen specification, Figma frame or design image with the project's existing tokens and components. Use when asked to implement a supplied design.

interface.shortDescription: Build UI from a browser, spec or design file

name: design-browser
description: Collect browser evidence for interface work. Use for reference browsing, rendered inspection, interaction QA, performance measurements or design comparison. Default to Playwright CLI; use Aside for research and general browsing.

interface.shortDescription: Route browser work and collect UI evidence

name: explain-interface
description: Explains how a website, a visual effect or an animation was built, from a live URL or a screenshot.

interface.shortDescription: How was this built? From a URL or a screenshot

name: information-architecture
description: Organize product content into destinations, labels and navigation. Use when mapping information architecture, a sitemap or findability from an agreed product brief, or restructuring an existing information hierarchy.

interface.defaultPrompt: Use $information-architecture for the scoped product design task and preserve existing decisions.

name: interface-review
description: Reviews a branch, pull request or uncommitted change for the interface problems it introduced or regressed, across accessibility, layout, writing, typography, color and UI.

interface.shortDescription: Branch, PR and working-tree interface review

name: prototype
description: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.

interface.shortDescription: Prototype to answer a design question

name: state-machine
description: Renders every state of a component you choose on a throwaway page, with mock data and a switcher, so you can work on each state.

interface.shortDescription: Every state of one component on a throwaway page, behind a switcher

name: user-flow
description: Design the actions, decisions and recovery paths for a product task. Use when mapping a user journey through screens or specifying task transitions before implementation, rather than displaying an existing component's coded states.

interface.shortDescription: Map task actions, branches and recovery
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $user-flow for the scoped product design task and preserve existing decisions.

name: variant
description: Builds multiple variants of a component you're working on and helps you iterate and pick one.

interface.shortDescription: Several versions of one UI piece behind a picker

name: wireframe
description: Turn agreed task flows and content into low-fidelity interactive screens and a Markdown screen specification. Use when deciding screen hierarchy, controls and responsive order before visual design or production implementation.

interface.defaultPrompt: Use $wireframe for the scoped product design task and preserve existing decisions.
